summary:
Abaddon gives hand-cast spells cascade on your turn, up to the life opponents have lost that turn. This review re-verifies the source's 63 KB interaction review and the retrospective attestation against current Oracle text, rulings and CR 2026-09-25. It also covers the refined list's Stormfist Crusader.

New findings:
- Abaddon's cascade is mandatory once a spell qualifies. It can send a card tutored to the top to the bottom, and any 0-MV spell cast on your turn randomizes your whole library. Both are sequencing hazards.
- The source's mana value for Call Forth the Tempest is wrong (8, not 11).

The Breach package is rules-coherent but finite and fuel-dependent.

interactions.title: Abaddon's threshold counts life opponents actually lost this turn
interactions.ruling: X is the total life all opponents have lost so far this turn, summed across opponents. It resets each turn. Damage to a player counts because damage causes life loss. Direct life loss counts too. Your own life payments (fetchlands, shocklands, Ancient Tomb, Mana Confluence, Force of Will's alternative cost, Flame Rift's damage to you) never count. Gaining life back later doesn't lower X: the text counts life lost, not the net change.
interactions.short: X = total life opponents lost this turn (damage counts; your own life payments don't).

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.

source.quote: The life-loss threshold is reset by the turn boundary; prior-turn life loss does not count.
The threshold uses life actually lost, not attempted/prevented damage.

interactions.title: Only spells cast from your hand, during your turn, get cascade
interactions.ruling: The grant needs all three: it is your turn, the spell is cast from your hand, and its mana value is ≤ X when cast. Spells cast from exile (cascade hits, Jeska's Will, Harnfel, The Ruinous Powers, Prosper, suspend, foretell), from the graveyard (Underworld Breach escape) or from the command zone (Abaddon himself) never get Abaddon's cascade. Their own printed cascade still works.
interactions.short: Hand-cast spells on your turn only; exile, graveyard and command-zone casts never get the grant.

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.

source.quote: Only spells cast from the controller's hand receive cascade from Abaddon.
A spell cast from exile by cascade is not cast from hand and does not receive Abaddon's grant

interactions.title: Eligibility is checked as the spell is cast; later life loss can't add cascade
interactions.ruling: Cascade is a cast trigger, so whether the spell has cascade is fixed when casting finishes. If a spell's own damage or life loss pushes X up after it resolves, that same spell does not gain cascade. Raise X first: ping with Thermo-Alchemist, let Loyal Subordinate's or Stormfist Crusader's triggers resolve, or resolve a Boltwave. Only then cast the spell that needs the higher threshold.
interactions.short: Build X before casting: a spell's own damage can't give it cascade retroactively.

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.
{T}: This creature deals 1 damage to each opponent.

rulings.quote: Cascade triggers when you cast the spell, meaning that it resolves before that spell.

source.quote: Abaddon checks the threshold as each spell is cast. Life loss caused by that spell after it has been cast cannot retroactively give that spell cascade.

interactions.title: Mana value, not the cost you paid, is what is compared
interactions.ruling: Abaddon and cascade both compare mana value, which comes only from the printed mana cost. Alternative costs (Fierce Guardianship, Deadly Rollick and Deflecting Swat for free, Force of Will's pitch) and cost reductions (Nightscape Familiar, Blasphemous Act's own discount) change what you pay, not mana value. A free Fierce Guardianship cast from your hand on your turn at X ≥ 3 has cascade and can hit a nonland card with MV 0–2. A free Deadly Rollick at X ≥ 4 can hit MV 0–3. Force of Negation's free mode works only on an opponent's turn, so its free cast never gets Abaddon's cascade.
interactions.short: Free/pitch casts still cascade at their printed MV; Force of Negation's free mode is opponent-turn only.

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.
If it's not your turn, you may exile a blue card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost.

rulings.quote: The mana value of the spell is determined only by its mana cost, no matter what the total cost to cast the spell was.

source.quote: The general rule is that **alternate cost changes what is paid, not mana value or the hand-cast zone condition**.

interactions.title: Cascade resolves before the spell that has it
interactions.ruling: Cascade triggers on cast and goes on the stack above its spell, so it resolves first. A cascaded Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal, Mystical Tutor, Brainstorm or Ponder can't set up the top card for its own cascade. The tutor's top-deck effect only applies after its cascade has already exiled cards.

rulings.quote: Cascade triggers when you cast the spell, meaning that it resolves before that spell.

source.quote: Cascade resolves before its source spell, so the cantrip/tutor cannot set up the top card for its own already-triggered cascade

interactions.title: A stacked top card is exposed to every later cascade on your turn
interactions.ruling: Under Abaddon, cascade is not optional. Once a hand-cast spell qualifies, the cascade must exile cards; you only choose whether to cast the hit. A card you put on top (Vampiric Tutor, Imperial Seal, Mystical Tutor, Brainstorm) is the first card the next cascade on your turn exiles. If it is a nonland card with lower mana value than the cascading spell, you may cast it for free, which is a strong line. Otherwise (a land, or MV equal or higher) it goes to the bottom in a random order and is lost for the turn. Sequence: draw it first, or cascade only from a spell with higher MV than the tutored card.
interactions.short: Tutoring to the top, then casting a qualifying spell, can send the tutored card to the bottom.

flag.note: Sequencing hazard, not a list error. Top-of-library tutors and Abaddon's mandatory cascade compete on your own turn. Pilot note: draw the tutored card first, or tutor on an opponent's end step.

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.

rulings.quote: When the cascade ability resolves, you must exile cards. The only optional part of the ability is whether or not you cast the last card exiled.

source.quote: A tutor that puts a card on top can therefore set up a later, higher-mana-value cascade spell.

interactions.title: Mana value 0 spells always qualify, and their cascade randomizes your library
interactions.ruling: X can't be negative, so Lion's Eye Diamond, Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox and Pact of Negation cast from your hand on your turn always have cascade. Cascade looks for a nonland card with mana value less than 0, which doesn't exist. You therefore exile your whole library, then put it all on the bottom in a random order. Nothing is cast, and any card you set up on top is randomized. The source review only noted that Pact 'gains no useful cascade hit'. The library randomization is an addition from this review.
interactions.short: 0-MV spells (LED, Petal, Mox, Pact) cascade into nothing and randomize your whole library.

flag.note: Pilot note: casting a 0-drop artifact or Pact from hand on your turn with Abaddon out effectively shuffles your library. Cast them before stacking the top, or on another turn. No list change: the cards are core fast mana.

oracle.quote: During your turn, spells you cast from your hand with mana value X or less have cascade, where X is the total amount of life your opponents have lost this turn.

source.quote: Pact of Negation remains different: its mana value is 0, so no card can have lower mana value than it; its cascade instance cannot find a legal card to cast.

interactions.title: Granted cascade stacks with printed cascade
interactions.ruling: Each cascade instance triggers separately. Bituminous Blast (MV 5) cast from hand on your turn at X ≥ 5 cascades twice, and each trigger looks for MV < 5. Call Forth the Tempest has **mana value 8** ({5}{R}{R}{R}), so at X ≥ 8 it gets a third instance. The archived review said 'mana value 11 ({8}{R}{R}{R})', which is wrong for current Oracle. Noise Marine (MV 5) gets two triggers at X ≥ 5. Each hit resolves above the original spell, so Blast's 4 damage resolves last.
interactions.short: Printed + granted cascade trigger separately (Bituminous Blast ×2, Call Forth ×3 at X ≥ 8).

flag.note: The source review's Call Forth the Tempest mana value (11) is wrong; current Oracle is MV 8, so the third instance needs X ≥ 8, not 11. No list change.

rulings.quote: the second cascade ability will look for a card with mana value less than Call Forth the Tempest's mana value of 8.

source.quote: **Call Forth the Tempest** has two printed instances of cascade and mana value 11 ({8}{R}{R}{R}).

interactions.title: Cards without a mana cost: cascade hits, never Abaddon casts
interactions.ruling: Ancestral Vision, Inevitable Betrayal and Profane Tutor have MV 0 and no mana cost, so they can't be cast from hand normally. Suspending them is a special action, not a cast. When suspend's last time counter comes off you may cast them from exile, which gets no Abaddon cascade. Any cascade with MV ≥ 1 can hit them and cast them for free. That is a cast from exile, so it triggers Keeper of Secrets, The Lost and the Damned, Prosper, Passionate Archaeologist, Wild-Magic Sorcerer and Nalfeshnee. Underworld Breach can't escape them: their escape cost includes an unpayable mana cost.

rulings.quote: A card with no mana cost can't be cast normally; you'll need a way to cast it for an alternative cost or without paying its mana cost, such as by suspending it.
Exiling a card with suspend isn't casting that card.
If a card has no mana cost, its escape cost is an unpayable cost, so you can't cast it for that cost.

source.quote: When cast from exile this way they are normal spell casts, not suspend casts.

interactions.title: Bloodletter and Solphim modify different events
interactions.ruling: Solphim doubles noncombat **damage** from your sources to opponents. Bloodletter doubles the **life loss** an opponent takes on your turn. They are replacement effects on different events, so both apply. Boltwave's 3 becomes 6 damage, which causes 12 life lost per opponent, so X = 36 at a three-opponent table. Flame Rift's 4 becomes 8 damage and 16 lost per opponent; the 4 it deals to you is not doubled. Bloodletter doesn't change damage, so lifelink gains only the damage dealt. Solphim does nothing for pure life loss (Loyal Subordinate, Stormfist Crusader, The Ruinous Powers).
interactions.short: Solphim doubles damage, Bloodletter doubles the resulting life loss: Boltwave → 12 per opponent.

oracle.quote: If an opponent would lose life during your turn, they lose twice that much life instead.
If a source you control would deal noncombat damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage to that player or permanent instead.

rulings.quote: Bloodletter of Aclazotz's last ability doesn't change the amount of damage dealt to opponents.

source.quote: These are replacement effects acting on different parts of damage/life loss.

interactions.title: Upkeep and combat life loss open the threshold early
interactions.ruling: Stormfist Crusader (added in the refined list) makes each player lose 1 at your upkeep. Each opponent loses 1, so X = 3 at a four-player table before your main phase, or 6 with Bloodletter. Your own 1 doesn't count. Loyal Subordinate makes each opponent lose 3 at beginning of combat if you control your commander as it resolves, so 9, or 18 with Bloodletter. That opens Abaddon cascades for post-combat main-phase spells. Both are life loss, not damage, so Solphim doesn't double them.
interactions.short: Stormfist (upkeep, 1 each) and Loyal Subordinate (combat, 3 each) build X without damage.
interactions.uncertainty: The exact X depends on table size (three opponents assumed) and on Stormfist also feeding opponents a card each turn; this is a strategic cost, not a rules question.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your upkeep, each player draws a card and loses 1 life.
At the beginning of combat on your turn, if you control your commander, each opponent loses 3 life.

interactions.title: Neheb converts the turn's life loss into post-combat mana
interactions.ruling: Neheb adds {R} for each 1 life opponents lost this turn, at the beginning of your postcombat main phase. It counts total life lost, not the net change in life totals. The trigger uses the stack (it is not a mana ability), and Neheb must be on the battlefield when that phase begins. Neheb's afflict is life loss, so it also raises X.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of each of your postcombat main phases, add {R} for each 1 life your opponents have lost this turn.

rulings.quote: Neheb's ability checks only how much life opponents lost during the turn, not by how much their life total decreased compared to the start of the turn.
Because it triggers at the beginning of a phase, Neheb's last ability isn't a mana ability.

interactions.title: Rakdos: castable only after life loss; reduces generic mana only
interactions.ruling: Rakdos can't be cast unless an opponent lost life this turn, and his discount doesn't apply to himself. Once he's out, creature spells cost {1} less per life opponents lost. The discount can't reduce colored pips and applies after cost increases like commander tax, so it can make Abaddon's recast cheaper. Reduced cost doesn't change mana value, so Abaddon's cascade comparison is unaffected.

oracle.quote: You can't cast Rakdos unless an opponent lost life this turn.

rulings.quote: Rakdos's last ability won't reduce the cost to cast Rakdos itself.
If there are additional costs to cast a creature spell, such as a kicker cost or the commander tax, apply those increases before applying cost reductions.
Rakdos's last ability can't reduce the colored mana requirement of a creature spell you cast.

interactions.title: Cast-from-exile payoffs see cascade hits but not copies
interactions.ruling: Each spell cast off a cascade, Jeska's Will, Harnfel, The Ruinous Powers, Prosper or Mind's Desire is a cast from exile. It triggers Keeper of Secrets (damage equal to its MV), Abaddon's Passionate Archaeologist ability (same), a Spawn from The Lost and the Damned, and a Treasure from Prosper. Nalfeshnee also copies it. Copies (Nalfeshnee, storm) are not cast and trigger none of these. Keeper and The Lost and the Damned also trigger on escape casts from the graveyard and on casting Abaddon from the command zone. Keeper's and Archaeologist's damage to opponents is damage, so it raises X and Solphim doubles it.
interactions.short: Exile casts trigger Keeper/Archaeologist/Lost and Damned/Prosper/Nalfeshnee; copies trigger none.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand, this creature deals damage equal to that spell's mana value to target opponent.
Commander creatures you own have "Whenever you cast a spell from exile, this creature deals damage equal to that spell's mana value to target opponent."
you cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand, create a 3/3 red Spawn creature token.

source.quote: Copies of a spell are not cast, so they do not trigger Keeper of Secrets.

interactions.title: Passionate Archaeologist works from the 99
interactions.ruling: Passionate Archaeologist is a Background, but the deck runs it as an ordinary enchantment in the 99, not as a second commander (Abaddon has no 'Choose a Background'). Its static ability gives the trigger to commander creatures you own, so Abaddon has it only while Abaddon is on the battlefield. A cast from exile while Abaddon is in the command zone or graveyard deals nothing.

rulings.quote: If you control a Background that grants an ability to commander creatures you own, and you own more than one commander creature, each of them will have that ability.

source.quote: Abaddon is a commander creature you own, so the Background gives Abaddon an ability that triggers when you cast a spell from exile.

interactions.title: Wild-Magic Sorcerer: only the first exile cast each turn cascades
interactions.ruling: The first spell you cast from exile each turn gets cascade, so the first cascade hit or Jeska's Will card can chain. Later exile casts that turn don't. If Sorcerer arrives after your first exile cast that turn, it gives nothing more that turn. Two Sorcerers would give that one spell two instances, but the deck has one.

interactions.title: Nalfeshnee copies exile casts; permanent copies are hasty, temporary tokens
interactions.ruling: Nalfeshnee copies each spell you cast from exile. A copied permanent spell becomes a token with haste that's sacrificed at end step. The copy isn't cast, so it gets no cascade and doesn't trigger Keeper, Archaeologist, Prosper, The Lost and the Damned or storm count. Storm-Kiln Artist does trigger on a copied instant or sorcery.

Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell, create a Treasure token.

interactions.title: Delayed Blast Fireball is the 5-damage version whenever it's cast from exile
interactions.ruling: Cast from exile for any reason (cascade hit, foretell, Jeska's Will, Harnfel, Prosper), it deals 5 to each opponent and their creatures. That is 15 life lost at a three-opponent table, 30 with Solphim, 60 with Solphim and Bloodletter. Cast from hand it deals 2, but it can get Abaddon's cascade at X ≥ 3. Foretelling is a special action that costs {2} on your turn.

rulings.quote: Delayed Blast Fireball deals 5 damage if it was cast from exile for any reason; it doesn't have to be from its foretell ability.

interactions.title: The Ruinous Powers: opponents' cards, life loss only after the cast
interactions.ruling: At your upkeep you exile a random opponent's top card. Until end of turn you may play it, with mana of any color. When you cast it, its owner (that opponent) loses life equal to its MV, which raises X, and Bloodletter doubles it. It's cast from exile, so it never gets Abaddon's cascade, and the life loss comes after the cast. Normal timing rules apply. A land played this way causes no life loss.

oracle.quote: When you cast a spell this way, its owner loses life equal to its mana value.

rulings.quote: You must follow all normal timing rules when casting a spell or playing a land using the permission granted by Ruinous Powers.

source.quote: The spell cast from The Ruinous Powers is from exile, not your hand, so Abaddon does not grant cascade to that spell.

interactions.title: Underworld Breach + Lion's Eye Diamond + Brain Freeze
interactions.ruling:
With Breach and LED on the battlefield and Brain Freeze in the graveyard:
1. Sacrifice LED for three mana of one color. LED's mana ability is instant-speed, and discarding your hand is part of its cost.
2. Escape LED for {0} plus three other graveyard cards.
3. Escape Brain Freeze for {1}{U} plus three cards.
Every escape is a cast, so storm grows. Storm copies aren't cast and don't add to storm. Mill yourself for fuel and finish by milling opponents.

Notes:
- Escape casts come from the graveyard, so none of them gets Abaddon's cascade.
- Milling an empty library doesn't make a player lose. They lose only when they try to draw from it (e.g. Wheel of Fortune or Windfall). Keep enough library to survive your own wheel.
- Breach is sacrificed at the end step.
- It is a resource-dependent finite loop with a fuel requirement, not a free infinite. The archived worked line needs at least six other cards across hand and graveyard.
interactions.short: Breach + LED + Brain Freeze: escape loop; mill alone doesn't win, Wheel/Windfall finishes.

oracle.quote: The escape cost is equal to the card's mana cost plus exile three other cards from your graveyard.

rulings.quote: The ability is a mana ability, so it is activated and resolves as a mana ability, but it can only be activated at times when you can cast an instant.
The copies are put directly onto the stack. They aren't cast and won't be counted by other spells with storm cast later in the turn.
Spells cast from zones other than a player's hand and spells that were countered are counted by the storm ability.

This is a resource-dependent finite-game combo sequence, not a resource-free mathematical infinite.

interactions.title: Breach + Lotus Petal + Brain Freeze
interactions.ruling: Lotus Petal's escape cost is {0} plus three cards. Each escape is a cast and nets one mana, so two Petal escapes pay for each Brain Freeze escape ({1}{U}) and add storm. The mill must keep returning at least nine cards per cycle (6 for the two Petals, 3 for Brain Freeze) to sustain the loop. The Spellbook record lists this as infinite self-mill and near-infinite mill. The same notes apply as for the LED line: no Abaddon cascade, and a mill finish needs a draw.

rulings.quote: If it is a permanent spell, it enters the battlefield and will return to its owner's graveyard if it dies later.

interactions.title: Breach + Wheel of Fortune (+ LED or Jeska's Will)
interactions.ruling: Each escaped Wheel discards everyone's hand and draws seven. That refills your graveyard, and opponents run out of library first if you've milled them. With LED, cracking LED in response pays for the next escaped Wheel ({2}{R} + 3 cards). With Jeska's Will, its mana mode (red for each card in a target opponent's hand, seven after a Wheel) plus its exile mode pay for and fuel the loop. Both modes need you to control a commander as you cast it. Drawing from an empty library is a loss at the next priority check. That is the kill, and also your own risk.

interactions.ruling: The 'both modes' check is made as you cast. Any commander you control counts, and losing it afterwards changes nothing. Cards played from the exile mode follow normal timing; a land needs an unused land drop. As casts from exile they trigger the exile payoffs but not Abaddon's cascade. Jeska's Will itself, cast from hand at X ≥ 3, can have cascade.

interactions.title: What the list depends on
interactions.ruling:
The deck wins in two ways:
- **Abaddon cascade turns:** these need X built before the big spells, with Boltwave, Thermo-Alchemist, Stormfist, Loyal Subordinate, the exile-damage creatures and Bloodletter doubling.
- **The Breach package:** it is commander-independent. Abaddon adds nothing to escape casts.

Both lines fold to graveyard hate and counters on key pieces. The interaction suite (Force of Will, Fierce Guardianship, Pact of Negation, Swan Song, Flusterstorm, Pyroblast, Deflecting Swat) protects them. Pact of Negation needs {3}{U}{U} at your next upkeep or you lose the game. If Pact is countered, the delayed trigger never happens.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your next upkeep, pay {3}{U}{U}. If you don't, you lose the game.

rulings.quote: If Pact of Negation is countered or otherwise doesn't resolve (perhaps because its target became illegal), the delayed triggered ability that threatens you with a game loss won't trigger at the beginning of your next upkeep.
